candidates.title: Don't expect scratchpad/CoT fine-tuning to extend compositional depth beyond training
candidates.rule: When deploying an LLM on exact multi-step algorithmic tasks (e.g., multi-digit multiplication, constraint puzzles, DP), do not rely on scratchpad prompting or scratchpad fine-tuning to generalize beyond the computation-graph depth/width seen in training; instead cap problem size at trained complexity or delegate to a tool/solver.
candidates.passage: GPT3 achieves near-perfect performance on in-distribution, but fails entirely in generalizing to OOD cases—in particular, wider or deeper computation graphs.
candidates.location: Section 3.1, 'Limits of transformers with explicit scratchpad training'
candidates.finding: Fine-tuning GPT3 (text-davinci-003) on question-scratchpad pairs gave near-perfect in-domain accuracy but near-zero accuracy on larger problem sizes; few-shot scratchpad prompting with GPT4 helped over zero-shot but decayed to zero as complexity grew.
workloads: Einstein's logic grid puzzles (K x M)
maximum weighted non-adjacent subsequence dynamic programming (length 2-10)
candidates.conditions: Fine-tuning on ~1.8M multiplication, ~142K DP, ~41K puzzle pairs; 500 test examples per task; nucleus p=0.7, temperature 1; evaluation Jan-May 2023; exact-match grading.
candidates.limitations: Only 2023-era OpenAI models and small open models; exact-match scoring of synthetic algorithmic tasks; one scratchpad linearization chosen among variants; no tool use or external planner baseline compared; results may not transfer to current reasoning-trained models.
candidates.validation_test: On a current model, fine-tune or few-shot prompt with scratchpads on k-by-k multiplication up to a fixed size, then measure exact accuracy on strictly larger sizes versus a calculator-tool baseline at matched cost.

candidates.title: Avoid extended post-overfitting training to buy OOD compositional generalization
candidates.rule: For compositional arithmetic fine-tuning, do not budget large amounts of extra training past the in-domain accuracy plateau in hopes of grokking-driven OOD generalization; stop at the plateau and spend the budget on decomposition or tooling instead.
candidates.passage: Figure 4 shows no improvement in generalization for OOD cases beyond the overfitting point, even after extensive training periods.
candidates.finding: GPT3 was fine-tuned for 420K steps (question-answer, ~60 epochs, $50,000) and 30K steps (question-scratchpad, 40 epochs, $40,000) on multiplication; no OOD gain appeared beyond overfitting.
candidates.conditions: Single task (multiplication) only, due to budget; OpenAI fine-tuning API, 2023; OOD defined as larger digit sizes than trained.
candidates.limitations: One task, one model, one training recipe; authors note they could not push data size or epochs further and speculate grokking might need different task difficulty or representations; no learning-rate or architecture sweep.
candidates.validation_test: Replicate on an open model: train on k-digit multiplication to the in-domain plateau, then continue for 10x more steps, tracking OOD accuracy at each checkpoint to see if any delayed generalization occurs.

reason: The paper tests scratchpad prompting/fine-tuning, exhaustive task-specific fine-tuning, and extended (grokking) training on three compositional tasks, reporting null results for out-of-distribution generalization. These support narrowly scoped rules about not relying on scratchpads/fine-tuning for compositional depth, and about decomposing work into few-step chunks. Theoretical error-propagation results are analytic, not empirical, so are framed as inferred.
